subject: Mutual action plan: performance eval results and variant selection
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jamal Harris <jamal.harris@acmehealth.io>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual action plan draft + initial perf targets

Jamal / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is v3 of the Mutual Action Plan (file: acme_MAP_v3.xlsx) — I updated the close timeline and added the perf evaluation milestones we discussed. Key items for your review: 

- Week 1: access + baseline test (sandbox tokens, shared eval data)
- Week 2: Redwood runs controlled performance sweep (latency, TTFT, throughput) across three candidate model variants
- Week 3: joint quality review and selection; procurement paperwork and PoC contract signature by EOD Friday Week 3

We set preliminary SLO targets to guide the sweep: P50 latency < 80 ms, P95 latency < 220 ms for 1k token generation; TTFT < 180 ms; sustained throughput target 150 rps at 32 concurrency. These are starting points — if your production profile skews shorter prompts/concurrency, we can re-run.

Next step: Jamal, can you confirm the eval dataset (medical notes + patient Q&A) will be uploaded to the shared Drive link by tomorrow EOD? Lauren / Neha — we'll own the perf sweep and deliver a one-pager with numeric results and a recommended variant.

Thanks,
Rishi
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Attachments: acme_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), performance_summary_qp.pdf (placeholder)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jamal Harris <jamal.harris@acmehealth.io>, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan draft + initial perf targets

Thanks Rishi — confirming receipt of the dataset this morning (I can see the Drive upload). I'll kick off the baseline harness today. Quick notes on test configs so expectations are aligned: 

- Test harness: 1k sample prompts representative of triage Q&A, median prompt length ~60 tokens, target generation length 300 tokens for quality evals.
- Variants to test (catalog names): rw-gpt-13b-v1, rw-gpt-7b-8bit-v2, rw-instruct-13b-qat (8-bit instruction-tuned).
- Perf sweep plan: single-node latency profiles (P50/P95), multi-client concurrency test at 8/16/32/64, and sustained throughput for 30-minute windows. We'll also report TTFT (time to first token) and tail behavior under burst.

I expect raw logs and CSV summary in 48 hours. If Acme wants different gen length for production, flag now (we can re-run shorter gen lengths quickly).

-L
Lauren Bishop
SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: variant_test_logs.tar.gz (logs & harness configs)
From: Jamal Harris <jamal.harris@acmehealth.io>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan draft + initial perf targets

Thanks Lauren — confirmed. One ask from procurement/security: can we include an additional variant that is quantized but not instruction-tuned (we want to compare raw generative fidelity vs tuned responses). Also, our production expected concurrency is closer to 24 sustained, with occasional spikes to 48. Please include a 24-concurrency steady-state in the report.

I'll get the signed NDA addendum over to procurement by EOD Friday.

-Jamal
Director of ML Ops, Acme Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jamal Harris <jamal.harris@acmehealth.io>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan draft + initial perf targets

Jamal — added the extra variant (rw-gpt-13b-4bit) to the sweep matrix. Quick preview of the numbers coming tomorrow after the first pass (raw experimental outputs, not final QA):

- rw-gpt-13b-v1: QA accuracy (internal eval) 91.8%, P50 latency 72 ms, P95 205 ms, TTFT 145 ms, throughput @24c 165 rps sustained
- rw-gpt-13b-4bit: QA 89.9%, P50 60 ms, P95 190 ms, TTFT 130 ms, throughput @24c 210 rps sustained
- rw-gpt-7b-8bit-v2: QA 86.7%, P50 48 ms, P95 150 ms, TTFT 110 ms, throughput @24c 270 rps sustained
- rw-instruct-13b-qat: QA 90.5%, P50 78 ms, P95 230 ms, TTFT 160 ms, throughput @24c 150 rps sustained

Notes: QA accuracy is measured on Acme's provided dev set with automated metrics + spot human checks (we'll provide the eval notebook). The 4-bit quant variant shows a good perf bump with modest quality drop; the 7b variant is fast but trails on clinical reasoning cases. We'll attach the raw confusion slices.

-Neha
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jamal Harris <jamal.harris@acmehealth.io>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan draft + initial perf targets

Adding a short engineering read: during the 64-concurrency spike test we saw graceful queuing with our prefix cache enabled, but the rw-instruct-13b-qat variant occasionally clipped at the token-emission rate under sustained long generations (300 tokens) — manifested as increased P95 but stable P50. For Acme, if most generations are under 200 tokens, the runtime impact is smaller.

Recommendation (engineer-first): if Acme values strict clinical accuracy on edge cases, choose rw-gpt-13b-v1 or the instruct-tuned 13b; if throughput/cost dominates, rw-gpt-13b-4bit is the best compromise; the 7b variant is an attractive low-cost fallback for non-critical routes.

I'll prepare a short slide (performance_delta_slide.pdf) summarizing tradeoffs for the MAP review on Monday.

-Karthik
Lead, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jamal Harris <jamal.harris@acmehealth.io>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.io>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan draft + initial perf targets

Jamal / procurement team — tidy final steps so we can lock Week 3 signature: 

1) Recommendation from Redwood: adopt rw-gpt-13b-4bit as the primary serving variant (balance of quality & perf) and run a canary on rw-gpt-13b-v1 for high-sensitivity clinical flows.
2) Proposed commercial: 12-month reserved capacity (guaranteed baseline) + burst pool for spikes. Pricing sketch attached in MAP v3.
3) Action items for Acme: confirm PO path and counter-sign by Fri 20 Feb; confirm whether any additional security evidence is needed (we have SOC2 + sample audit logs ready).

If procurement confirms the PO cadence, we'll schedule the canary rollout plan and start onboarding in the Dedicated sandbox on Mon Feb 23.

Thanks — Rishi
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
summary: Thread contains MAP coordination and a performance sweep across four Redwood catalog variants. Internal team provides numeric results (latency, TTFT, throughput) and a recommended selection: rw-gpt-13b-4bit as primary with rw-gpt-13b-v1 for critical paths. Timeline targets a Week-3 signature and onboarding in Dedicated sandbox on Feb 23.
